subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Sri Lankan Ceylon Tea
description: A short lesson to help you apply Sri Lankan Ceylon Tea.

hook.text: Sri Lanka was a coffee island until 1869 when leaf rust destroyed every plantation. Tea replaced it entirely.

buildup.text: Scottish planter James Taylor planted the first tea in 1867. Within decades, Ceylon tea was a global export brand.

discovery.text: Sri Lanka is the world's 4th-largest tea producer. Tea accounts for 15% of export revenue and employs 1 million people.

twist.text: The name 'Ceylon' on tea labels refers to Sri Lanka's colonial name—a brand identity the tea board deliberately preserved.

climax.text: Ceylon tea ranges from low-country bold to high-country delicate. Altitude defines character, just like wine regions.

punchline.text: Coffee died, tea rose. Sri Lanka turned disaster into global brand.

quiz.question: Why did Sri Lanka switch from coffee to tea?
options: Coffee leaf rust destroyed all plantations in the 1860s–1870s

details.summary: Sri Lanka, formerly Ceylon, produces distinctive black teas known for their bright, brisk character. Tea growing began after coffee rust destroyed the island's coffee plantations in the 1870s.
details.whyItMatters: Ceylon tea is one of the world's most recognized tea brands. An entire national economy was rebuilt on tea after agricultural disaster, a remarkable story of resilience.
takeaways: Sri Lanka produces bright, brisk black teas called Ceylon tea
Tea replaced coffee after the 1870s rust epidemic destroyed crops
Seven elevation regions produce distinct flavor profiles

faq.question: What makes Ceylon tea different from Indian tea?
faq.answer: Ceylon teas are generally brighter and more citrusy than Assam's malty heaviness or Darjeeling's muscatel character. The island's varied elevations create remarkable range: low-grown teas are strong and full, mid-grown are smooth, and high-grown Nuwara Eliya teas are light, floral, and prized.

faq.question: How important is tea to Sri Lanka's economy?
faq.answer: Tea is Sri Lanka's most valuable agricultural export, contributing over a billion dollars annually. It employs over a million people directly and indirectly. The tea industry is central to the country's economy, culture, and international identity. The Ceylon tea brand is recognized worldwide.
